method: Per host country and year (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 = Jan-Aug), public cost of hosting refugees from Ukraine, EUR bn, low/central/high (~90% interval). (1) Person-years: EU/EFTA from Eurostat migr_asytpsm monthly stock (average of monthly stocks /12; missing early-2022 months back-filled with the EU ramp); other countries from UNHCR end-year counts (refugees + asylum seekers): 2022 = end-2022 x 0.7125 (EU ramp Mar-Dec 2022), 2023-2025 = mean of start and end of year, 2026 Jan-Aug = end-2025 x 0.6729. USA (Uniting for Ukraine + border parole) and Canada (CUAET arrivals) use programme figures instead of UNHCR. (2) Reported basis (B): Germany (federal), Poland (Aid Fund), Czechia (Labour Ministry gross), Netherlands (central-government schemes), Switzerland (federal lump sum x person-years). Comprehensive scopes (CZE, NLD): central = reported; partial scopes (DEU, POL, CHE): low = reported, high = reported x documented scope gap, central = geometric mean. (3) Modelled basis (C): cost = person-years x k x GDP per head, k calibrated on 16 reported country-years (DEU, POL, CZE, NLD 2022-2025): log-normal fit, k = 0.0479 / 0.1524 / 0.4852 (low/central/high). Reported partial spending (Ireland accommodation, UK Homes for Ukraine, Canada transitional assistance) is a floor. Countries with no UNHCR record get zero.

calibration.unit: k = cost per refugee person-year / GDP per head (World Bank 2024, EUR)
calibration.fit: log-normal over the 16 country-year points; low/high = exp(mean +/- 1.645 sd), i.e. a ~90% interval

ramp.r22_meaning: 2022 person-years per end-2022 refugee (Eurostat EU/EFTA, Mar-Dec 2022)
ramp.g26_meaning: Jan-Aug 2026 person-years per Dec-2025 refugee (Eurostat EU/EFTA)

notes: Our EU-27 total for 2022-2025 is EUR 100.9bn (range 64.6-196.9), against Kiel's EUR 163.1bn (EPRS 775834 Fig. 6). Kiel's figure implies ~EUR 10,850 per person-year (k = 0.288), which sits inside our range but above our central. Kiel builds per-country costs from OECD first-year cost estimates and asylum-cost averages rather than budget outturns. National budget figures (Czechia, Poland's Aid Fund, German federal) come out 2-3x lower than the Kiel/OECD modelled values for the same countries.

Kiel per-country figures seen via secondary sources (Statista, Mar 2022-Feb 2025: Germany 36.6, Spain 8.6, Ireland 3.06, Norway 3.03 EUR bn; press: Poland 29.3, Czechia 8.0 to Aug 2025) are modelled, not reported spending. They are used here only to set the upper bound for partial-scope countries.

Poland's count is far below the often-quoted 1.5m. Eurostat temporary protection peaked at 1.37m (Sep 2022) and was 0.96m in Dec 2022, after PESEL deregistrations. UNHCR end-2022 = 0.96m. 2022 Polish person-years = 0.91m.

Germany's Eurostat series starts Aug 2022 (680k). Mar-Jul 2022 is back-filled, so 2022 person-years (0.56m) may be understated. This affects only the calibration point, because Germany's cost is reported.

Russia is excluded from 'countries' because it is not in the refugee-hosting gap list. UNHCR showed 1,275,315 (end-2022) and 1,227,554 (end-2023) Ukrainians in Russia, based on Russian government data, then 6,894 (end-2024) and 5,488 (end-2025). Many were deported or forcibly transferred, so a hosting cost would not count as support to Ukraine.
Italy's Eurostat stock drops from 162k (Dec 2024) to 60k (Dec 2025) after a records clean-up, so 2025-26 Italian costs fall with it.

Canada: UNHCR shows only 75k for 2022-2024, but more than 298k CUAET holders had arrived by Apr 2024. The USA has 3.3k UNHCR refugees but about 240k U4U parolees plus 30-35k border parolees. Programme counts are used for both, with wider count bands.

OECD DAC in-donor refugee costs (all nationalities, first 12 months only, USD m, DAC1 measure 1820) are kept as a cross-check, not as an input: e.g. POL 2193 (2022), DEU 4809/7286/6254 (2022-24), GBR 4549/5311, IRL 1205/1473, CHE 1264/1460, NLD 946/1297, CZE 646/418, CAN 923/1690, USA 7784/6953. k uses 2024 GDP per head for every year. Ireland's GDP per head is inflated by multinationals, so its modelled high bound is generous. Reported accommodation spending is used as Ireland's floor.
